Profitability $0.7B GAAP operating income $0.8B GAAP net income $1.7B non-GAAP net income1 In Q3, we maintained strong momentum on many projects spanning Super Intelligence (SI), robotics and renewable energy that will be critical to building a future of Amazing Abundance. Strength in our core business also continued, and we achieved our second consecutive quarter of TTM revenue in excess of $100B. deliveries in North America – our most mature market – a nearly twenty percentage point sequential increase. We believe that FSD is driving demand in markets where it is available, and we continue to work with regulators to get it approved in other markets. We started providing Robotaxi rides using Cybercabs on September 3 in Austin. Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew eightfold quarter over quarter, driven by sustained double-digit weekly growth. We ended the quarter with the largest backlog for our passenger vehicles in four years. We rolled out the updated Tesla Semi that is produced on our high-volume manufacturing line in Nevada and unveiled the Next Gen Roadster on October 15. While battery availability continued to be the limiting factor in increasing auto volumes in the quarter, we have made additional progress in securing future supply, as we work toward our goal of maximum utilization of our factories. Demand for our Energy Storage business remained strong in the quarter, with our highest- ever order rate and backlog. Energy storage is the fastest way to add power to the existing grid and is critical to data center uptime. We expect rising data center demand to continue driving demand for our products. Megafactory Texas began production, with planned capacity of 50 GWh. We also advanced LFP supply domestication in the U.S., shipping the first Megapacks built with LFP cells from our factory in Nevada. We continue to invest in the future through R&D and Capex spend across our businesses, including SI, robotics and energy. Much hard work lies ahead, but we are as optimistic as ever. Thank you to our supporters as we continue to execute on many challenging and important projects. Automotive We achieved record quarterly deliveries in several markets, including Canada, Australia, Japan and Taiwan. Given the strong demand we are seeing across various markets, we remain focused on increasing production across our factories and attained record production at Gigafactory Berlin. We began volume production of Tesla Semi, our Class 8 heavy-duty truck. The top variant can go 500 miles at full 82,000 lbs gross combination weight while achieving an efficiency of 1.7 kWh/mile. That efficiency allows the Tesla Semi to use a third of the energy used by a comparable diesel truck to haul the same payload. In a transportation market where energy is one of the largest components of total cost per mile, this will provide a meaningful advantage to Tesla Semi operators. Energy Generation and Storage We began production at Megafactory Texas. Energy storage demand is increasingly aligned with SI infrastructure demand as grid constraints and power availability create more opportunities for Megapack to be deployed. Megapack excels in off-grid and on-grid applications, supplying large data center loads, buffering oscillating demand, helping interconnection grid-compliance and strengthening the grid – all with less local fossil fuel generation. Robotics Optimus production began in Fremont on our high-volume lines. The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured. While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product. 6 S U P P O R T I N G I N F R A S T R U C T U R E Installed Capacity Region Asset Capacity Status SI Training Compute1 Texas Cortex 1 >105 MW Production Cortex 2 >120 MW Production Battery Cell Manufacturing Annual Capacity Nevada LFP 7 GWh Early Ramp Texas 4680 >40 GWh Production Cathode Materials 10 GWh Early Ramp Lithium Refining 30 GWh Early Ramp Berlin 4680 - Construction approach capacity. SI Compute We plan to reach 400 MW of SI training compute by the end of the year, supporting the development of both vehicle and humanoid robot autonomy software. Additionally, we continued construction for the Austin Fab, where we plan to start commissioning equipment in 2027. Battery We continue to make progress expanding battery manufacturing capacity and securing future supply, even as battery availability remains a limiting factor on the pace of our global vehicle production ramp. Critical projects include vehicle pack capacity in Berlin, cathode material production and lithium refining in Texas and LFP cells in Nevada for our energy storage products. We shipped the first Megapacks comprised solely of our own LFP cells, an important milestone to localizing this important battery type. We continue to increase production of our 4680 cells to support the ramps of both Cybercab and Tesla Semi along with higher Model Y volumes. Other Supporting Infrastructure -over- year. Our Supercharger for Business program also grew to over 600 stalls. These customer- owned chargers allow us to further scale the charging network while ensuring the same performance standards and service standard as Tesla-owned locations. We deployed our first Accordion Supercharger, which is pre-assembled in the factory and cheaper to install. We also deployed the first pre-assembled Megacharger to support the Tesla Semi ramp. 7 Tesla SI Training Capacity Ramp (MW of Compute) 0 50 100 150 200 250 300 350 400 450 Existing Capacity Future Planned Capacity (1) Excludes 40 MW of other compute not part of Cortex 1 or Cortex 2. reference.summary: Tesla, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, leases, and sells electric vehicles, and energy generation and storage systems in the United States, China, and internationally. The company operates in two segments, Automotive; and Energy Generation and Storage. The company offers electric vehicles, as well as sells automotive regulatory credits; and non-warranty maintenance services and collision, automotive insurance services, as well as part sales and retail merchandise sale. It also provides sedans and sport utility vehicles through direct and used vehicle sales, a network of Tesla Superchargers, and in-app upgrades; purchase financing and leasing services; services for electric vehicles through its company-owned service locations and Tesla mobile service technicians; and vehicle limited warranties and extended service plans.
